newsitem.title: UK: Dollar trading winds up in pre-Christmas Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar trading winds up in pre-Christmas Europe.

text.p: Foreign exchange trading was grinding to a halt in Europe as traders left their desks early for the two-day Christmas break.

All major European centres are closed on Wednesday and Thursday with the exception of France which will be open on Thursday. Friday will be extremely quiet as many European dealers turn the two-day holiday into a long weekend.
At 1354 GMT the dollar was at 1.5545/51 marks and 114.30/35, barely changed from the early 1.5550/57 and 114.36/46. It closed on Monday at 1.5550 and 114.01/11.
There were no U.S. economic data today, but earlier Japan's index of leading indicators was reported at 83.3 in October, above the so-called boom-or-bust level of 50 for the second consecutive month.
A figure above 50 is generally taken as suggesting that the economy will expand in the coming months.
Analysts noted that the coincident and lagging index also rose and this is the first time since February 1996 that all three have risen above 50 in the same month.
This is a sign that the economy is getting closer to the self-sustaining recovery stage, they said.

The mark was steady on the crosses with mark/Paris showing little reaction to news that the French October trade surplus was 16.94 billion francs against the 10.6 billion forecast and revised 9.7 billion in September.
Sterling was below earlier highs on profit taking despite U.K. trade data coming in better than had been expected and the global shortfall narrowing sharply.
October's global trade deficit was just 454 million sterling against market forecasts for a 659 million shortfall and September's revised 1.06 billion deficit.
Traders noted that with the last U.K. economic data of this year now out of the way investors had banked profits made during sterling's recent strong rally.
Sterling was at 2.6011/22 marks against Monday's 2.6010/20 with cable at $1.6728/38 against a previous $1.6708/13. It earlier touched high of 2.6088 and $1.6780.
